mainTopic: Gentile inheritance by תורה law, and the differences between an עבד עברי and an אמה העבריה: יעוד, selling a thief twice, and redeeming her against the father's will.
overview: This amud opens with the last line of an earlier answer, about a son conceived before his mother converted and born after. Next, רבי יוחנן teaches that a נכרי inherits from his father by תורה law. The proof from עשו is pushed off, so the גמרא proves it from the children of לוט instead. The גמרא then explains why רבא and רב חייא בר אבין each prefer their own source. Then a ברייתא lists differences between an עבד עברי and an אמה העבריה. Its lines are examined one by one: רב ששת explains the case of a maidservant the master married (יעוד). רבא and אביי argue about whether a thief can be sold twice. A ברייתא about a thief worth more or less than his theft leads רבא to side with רבי אליעזר. Finally, 'against his will' is explained as the father's will, because of family shame. That rule depends on רבי שמעון, who holds that a daughter cannot be sold into servitude twice. The amud ends as the גמרא begins tracing this dispute to the פסוק 'בבגדו בה', which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Second case: conceived before conversion, born after
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an answer from the earlier discussion. 'Here' means a son whose mother conceived him before she converted but gave birth after she converted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, it is talking about someone who was conceived not in holiness, but was born in holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer that started before this section. It separates two cases, and this line gives the second one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A son conceived before his mother converted but born after she converted is in an in-between situation. He was born a Jew, yet he started life as a gentile's child. In this case, the money is returned to him.

keyTerms.meaning: His conception, meaning when his mother became pregnant with him
In holiness, meaning after the mother converted and was already Jewish

steps.confusionAlert: 'In holiness' here does not mean anything about how holy the parents were. It only means whether the mother was already Jewish (a גיורת) at that moment.

phrases.english: And here, where he was conceived not in holiness,
but his birth was in holiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a two-part answer that began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is talking about a different situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: This source is talking about a son conceived before his mother converted and born after.

steps.title: A gentile inherits his father: proof from עשו
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין quotes רבי יוחנן: by תורה law a נכרי inherits from his father. The proof is that ה׳ gave הר שעיר to עשו as an inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A gentile inherits from his father by תורה law. As it says: 'For I have given הר שעיר to עשו as an inheritance.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens. A gentile inheriting his father is a real תורה law, and the proof comes from a פסוק about עשו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls עשו's land a 'יְרֻשָּׁה', an inheritance. That word suggests that inheritance law works for him. Since עשו is usually thought of as a non-Jew, this would show that gentiles inherit by תורה law.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law, as opposed to a rabbinic rule

steps.whyThisMatters: If gentile inheritance comes from the תורה itself, it is a real legal right and not just a custom.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: נׇכְרִי יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אָבִיו דְּבַר תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: A gentile inherits from his father by Torah law,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי יְרֻשָּׁה לְעֵשָׂו נָתַתִּי אֶת הַר שֵׂעִיר״.
phrases.english: as it is written: “For I have given Mount Seir to Esau as an inheritance.”

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: gentile inheritance and where it comes from in the תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By תורה law, a נכרי inherits from his father.

steps.title: Maybe עשו counts as a Jew who left
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof. עשו was the son of יצחק, so he might count as a ישראל משומד, and that case could be different.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe an apostate Jew is different?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from עשו. He might not be a true gentile at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עשו was the son of יצחק and grandson of אברהם. So he might count as a Jew who left the path, a ישראל משומד. A Jew, even one who left, certainly inherits. So עשו's inheritance proves nothing about real gentiles.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jew who abandoned Judaism, an apostate

phrases.english: But perhaps an apostate Jew is different?
phrases.notes: The idea is that עשו, as יצחק's son, might count as a Jew who strayed, not a real gentile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes off the proof brought in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from עשו is rejected. The rule itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: עשו may count as a ישראל משומד, so he is not a clear example of a gentile.

steps.title: Better proof: the children of לוט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new proof. ה׳ gave the land of ער to the children of לוט as an inheritance, and they were definitely gentiles.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof is from here: 'For I have given ער to the children of לוט as an inheritance.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא swaps the weak proof for a stronger one, the children of לוט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The children of לוט (מואב) were never part of the Jewish family line in any way. So nobody could call them Jews who left. Since the פסוק still calls their land a 'יְרֻשָּׁה', this shows that real gentiles inherit by תורה law.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from here: a formula for bringing a replacement proof
The children of לוט, the nation of Moav

phrases.english: Rather, from here:

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּי לִבְנֵי לוֹט נָתַתִּי אֶת עָר יְרֻשָּׁה״.
phrases.english: “For I have given Ar to the children of Lot as an inheritance.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof that was rejected in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a נכרי inherits from his father by תורה law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 2:9, where the land of ער is given to the children of לוט as a יְרֻשָּׁה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule stands: a gentile inherits by תורה law. The proof is from the children of לוט, not from עשו.

steps.title: Why not use רבא's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב חייא בר אבין did not prove the same rule the way רבא did, from 'וחשב עם קונהו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חייא בר אבין: what is the reason he did not say it like רבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a comparison between two sources for the same rule. First it asks about רב חייא בר אבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבא proved gentile inheritance from the פסוק about a Jewish servant sold to a gentile: 'וְחִשַּׁב עִם קֹנֵהוּ'. If רבא's source works, why did רב חייא בר אבין need a different one?

keyTerms.meaning: Did not say it like (another sage)

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin,
what is the reason he did not say it like Rava?
phrases.notes: רבא's proof was given earlier, from the פסוק 'וחשב עם קונהו', ויקרא 25:50.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the proof in step 4 with רבא's proof from earlier.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב חייא בר אבין did not rely on רבא's proof from 'וחשב עם קונהו'.

steps.title: רבא's proof is only an inference
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק never actually says 'and not with the heirs of his buyer'. רבא's proof is only something read into the פסוק, not stated outright.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written: 'He shall reckon with his buyer, and not with the heirs of his buyer'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב חייא בר אבין. רבא's source does not say the rule openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's proof works by reasoning: since the פסוק says 'his buyer', it must exclude the buyer's heirs. That would mean the heirs would otherwise have inherited. But the words 'not with the heirs' are not actually in the פסוק. רב חייא בר אבין prefers a פסוק that openly uses the word 'יְרֻשָּׁה'.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written? A rhetorical question meaning 'it is not written'
He shall reckon with his buyer: the servant settles the account with the one who bought him

phrases.english: Is it written: “And he shall reckon with his buyer
and not with the heirs of his buyer”?
phrases.notes: The second half is not in the פסוק at all. The גמרא is pointing out that it is missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא's proof is only an inference. The פסוק never openly excludes the heirs, so it is not a clear source.

steps.title: Why not use רב חייא בר אבין's source?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא asks the opposite question: why didn't רבא use the פסוקים about עשו and לוט?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא: what is the reason he did not say it like רב חייא בר אבין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around. Now it asks why רבא did not use the openly stated proof from לוט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from לוט's children seems stronger, because the פסוק openly says 'יְרֻשָּׁה'. So רבא must have had a reason not to rely on it.

phrases.english: And Rava, what is the reason he did not say it
like Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the question in step 5, from רבא's side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבא did not rely on the proof from עשו and לוט.

steps.title: עשו and לוט were special because of אברהם
steps.stepSummary: The answer: עשו and לוט were both relatives of אברהם. They may have received land as an honor to him, which proves nothing about gentiles in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the honor of אברהם, it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבא. The land given to עשו and לוט might have been a special gift for אברהם's sake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עשו was אברהם's grandson, and לוט was his nephew. ה׳ may have given their families land out of respect for אברהם. That would be a special exception, not proof of a general inheritance law for all gentiles. So רבא prefers his own source, which talks about any gentile buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: אברהם אבינו, the relative of both עשו and לוט

steps.whatToRemember: Both sages agree that a gentile inherits by תורה law. They only disagree about which פסוק proves it. רב חייא בר אבין wants a פסוק that says it openly. רבא is worried that עשו and לוט were special because of אברהם.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא tests a proof. It checks whether the wording is open or only implied, and whether the example is typical or a special case.

phrases.english: Because of the honor of Abraham, it is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The inheritance of עשו and לוט may have been a special honor for אברהם, so it does not prove a general rule for gentiles.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists differences between a Hebrew slave and a Hebrew maidservant
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three ways only an עבד עברי goes free, and three things that apply only to an אמה העבריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: some things are true of a Hebrew slave but not of a Hebrew maidservant, and some are true of her but not of him. He goes free after six years, at the יובל, and when his master dies, but she does not. She goes free when she shows signs of maturity, she is not sold a second time, and she can be redeemed against 'his' will, but he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא that compares the עבד עברי with the אמה העבריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes two lists. The first is three ways out that only the man has: six years, the יובל, and the master's death. The second is three rules that only the woman has: signs of maturity, no second sale, and forced redemption. The next steps will question items on both lists.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish man sold as a servant
A Jewish girl sold by her father as a maidservant
The 50th year, when Hebrew servants go free
Physical signs that a girl has reached maturity

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
There are things with a Hebrew slave that are not with a Hebrew maidservant,
and there are things with a Hebrew maidservant that are not with a Hebrew slave.
With the Hebrew slave: he goes free through years,
and through the Jubilee year, and through the death of the master,
which is not so with the Hebrew maidservant.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ בָּעִבְרִיָּה, שֶׁהֲרֵי עִבְרִיָּה יוֹצְאָה בְּסִימָנִין
phrases.english: And there are things with the maidservant: for a Hebrew maidservant goes free through signs of maturity,
and she is not sold a second time,
and they may redeem her against his will,
phrases.notes: Whose will? The גמרא asks this later. רבא first says the master's, but אביי shows it means the father's.

phrases.english: which is not so with the Hebrew slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of gentile inheritance closed in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the עבד עברי goes free through years, the יובל, and the master's death. Only the אמה העבריה goes free through signs, is never sold a second time, and can be redeemed against 'his' will (explained in steps 22-24 as the father's will).

steps.title: The משנה says the maidservant has everything the slave has, plus more
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says she lacks some of his ways of going free, but the משנה implies she has all of them plus one extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: some things are true of a Hebrew slave but not of a Hebrew maidservant. But this contradicts the משנה: 'A Hebrew maidservant has more than him, since she acquires herself through signs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first line of the ברייתא and sets it against our משנה, which seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's words 'more than him' imply that she has every way out that he has (years, יובל, master's death), plus signs. So how can the ברייתא say she lacks those three ways?

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction

phrases.english: The Master said:
There are things with a Hebrew slave that are not with a Hebrew maidservant.
And this was contradicted:
A Hebrew maidservant has more than him,
since she acquires herself through signs!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first half of the ברייתא from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the עבד עברי has ways out that the אמה העבריה lacks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's phrase 'more than him' means she has all of his ways out plus signs, so she cannot be missing any of his.

steps.title: רב ששת: the ברייתא is talking about a maidservant the master married
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא refers to a case where the master did יעוד, making her his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: the case is one where the master designated her as his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת resolves the contradiction by narrowing the case the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the master does יעוד, she is his wife, and she no longer goes free through years, the יובל, or his death. The משנה is speaking of a regular maidservant, and the ברייתא of one who became a wife, so they do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: The master's designating the maidservant as his wife
For example; here, 'we are dealing with a case where'

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
For example, where he designated her.
phrases.notes: He means the master took her as his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to describe every Hebrew maidservant.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא describes only a maidservant whom the master designated as his wife.

steps.title: If she is his wife, isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: A married woman obviously needs a גט, so why would the ברייתא bother to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he designated her, it's obvious! She needs a גט!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's answer: in his case, the ברייתא would be teaching something everyone already knows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she is his wife, of course years or the יובל cannot end a marriage, since only a גט can. If that is the ברייתא's case, it seems to teach nothing new.

phrases.english: If he designated her, it is obvious!
She needs a bill of divorce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's answer from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the ברייתא is about a designated maidservant.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wife obviously needs a גט to leave, so the ברייתא would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: It is needed: you might have thought her servant rules still apply
steps.stepSummary: Without the ברייתא, one might think the old ways out of servitude still free her even after יעוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that the servant laws are not cancelled for her, so she could still go free like a servant. The ברייתא teaches that they are cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא is not stating the obvious; it blocks a mistaken idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could have thought that since she entered the house as a servant, her servant ways out (years, יובל, master's death) remain in place even after marriage. The ברייתא teaches that once she is designated, those rules no longer apply to her.

keyTerms.meaning: What might you have said? It introduces a mistaken idea
It teaches us (that it is not so)

phrases.english: You might have said
that the laws are not cancelled from her,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'cancel.'

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it's obvious' challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her servant ways out might still apply even after יעוד.
steps.terutzMaskana: After יעוד her servant ways out are cancelled; only a גט ends the marriage.

steps.title: Then how can a married maidservant go free through signs?
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא is about a designated maidservant, she should not go free through signs either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the ברייתא say she goes free through signs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with רב ששת's reading, this time from the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she is a wife, signs of maturity should no more free her than years or the יובל do. Yet the ברייתא lists signs as her special way out.

phrases.english: If so,
why does she go free through signs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a second challenge to רב ששת's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's reading, set against the ברייתא's line that she goes free through signs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A designated wife needs a גט, so signs should not free her either.

steps.title: The signs rule is about a maidservant who was not designated
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means that if there was no יעוד, she goes free through signs as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא is saying: if he did not designate her, she goes free also through signs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the second half of the ברייתא so that it fits רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's two halves describe different situations. The first half (she lacks his ways out) is about a designated maidservant. The signs rule is about one who was not designated, and the word 'also' shows that she has signs on top of his ways out.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means to say

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's first half is about a maidservant whom the master married (יעוד), so only a גט frees her. Its signs rule is about one who was not married, and she goes free through signs in addition to the slave's ways.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
If he did not designate her,
she goes free also through signs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 and closes the discussion of the first half of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The signs rule seemed to be about the same designated maidservant.
steps.terutzMaskana: The signs rule is about a maidservant who was not designated, and she goes free through signs as well as his ways.

steps.title: Can a Hebrew slave really be sold a second time?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא implies a man can be sold twice, but another ברייתא says a thief can be sold only once.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said 'she is not sold a second time'. That implies a Hebrew slave can be sold a second time? But a ברייתא teaches: 'for his theft' means not for his double payment. 'For his theft' means not for his false-witness payment. 'For his theft' means once he was sold one time, you may not sell him again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the first ברייתא and shows that it seems to clash with another ברייתא. The next step gives רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the woman cannot be sold twice, the man apparently can. But the second ברייתא learns from the פסוק 'for his theft' that a thief is sold only to repay the theft itself, not the כפל fine and not the payment of an עד זומם, and only once.

keyTerms.meaning: The double payment a thief pays as a fine
His plotting; the payment of a false witness (עד זומם)

phrases.english: "And she is not sold a second time."
This implies that a Hebrew slave can be sold a second time?
But isn't it taught:
"For his theft": and not for his double payment.
"For his theft": and not for his plotting.
phrases.notes: He means a false witness who must pay what he tried to cost someone else; he is not sold for that.

phrases.english: "For his theft":
once he has been sold one time,
you are no longer permitted to sell him again.

steps.confusionAlert: This step only raises the problem. רבא answers it in step 17, and אביי gives a different answer in step 19.
steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלַל דְּעֶבֶד עִבְרִי נִמְכָּר וְנִשְׁנֶה וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the ברייתא from step 9 and challenges what it implies.
steps.kashyaTarget: What the ברייתא implies: that an עבד עברי can be sold a second time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא learns from 'for his theft' that a thief can be sold only once, so a man cannot be sold twice either, and this would not be a difference between them.

steps.title: רבא: one theft versus two thefts
steps.stepSummary: רבא settles the contradiction. A single theft allows only one sale, while two separate thefts allow a second sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is not a contradiction. The ברייתא that says he is sold only once is talking about one theft. The ברייתא that allows a second sale is talking about two thefts.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction from Step 16 by saying each ברייתא is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a man stole once and his sale did not cover the whole debt, he cannot be sold again for the rest. If he was sold, then stole a second time, a new sale is allowed for the new theft. So both ברייתות are true, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources do not really contradict

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult.
Here, it is talking about one theft;
phrases.notes: "Here" is the ברייתא that says a thief is sold only once.

phrases.english: there, it is talking about two thefts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא covers a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seem to disagree about whether a thief can be sold twice
steps.terutzMaskana: One theft allows one sale. Two thefts allow two sales.

steps.title: אביי: 'for his theft' can mean many thefts
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבא's answer. The פסוק's word בגניבתו can cover many thefts, so even several thefts should allow only one sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The word "for his theft" means even many thefts.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's answer, using the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says he is sold "for his theft," and that phrase can include several thefts together. So the number of thefts cannot be what decides between one sale and two. רבא's split between the cases falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: For his theft; the wording of the פסוק about selling a thief

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
"For his theft" means many!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's answer from Step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the split between one theft and two thefts
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק's word בגניבתו covers many thefts, so the number of thefts cannot decide how many times he is sold

steps.title: אביי: one victim versus two victims
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives his own answer. Thefts from one person allow only one sale, while thefts from two different people allow two sales.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: It is not a contradiction. The ברייתא that says only one sale is talking about stealing from one person. The ברייתא that allows a second sale is talking about stealing from two people.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רבא, אביי offers a different way to split the two ברייתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What decides the matter is the number of victims, not the number of thefts. If all the thefts were from the same person, he is sold once, even for many thefts. If he stole from two different people, each victim can have him sold.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; turning from a rejected answer to a new one
Two people, meaning two different victims

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, a thief is sold once for everything he stole from one person, but he can be sold again for stealing from a different person.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said: It is not difficult.
Here, it is talking about one person;
phrases.notes: He means he stole from only one victim, even if he did it many times.

phrases.english: there, it is talking about two people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's rejected answer with a new split between the cases
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא) by the number of victims
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Splitting by the number of thefts does not work, because בגניבתו covers many thefts
steps.terutzMaskana: Thefts from one person allow one sale. Thefts from two people allow two sales.

steps.title: ברייתא: when the thief's value does not match what he stole
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches two cases. If the theft is worth more than the thief, he is sold and sold again. If the theft is worth less than the thief, he is not sold at all. רבי אליעזר says he is sold only when the theft equals his value.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If he stole a thousand and he is worth five hundred, he is sold and then sold again. If he stole five hundred and he is worth a thousand, he is not sold at all. רבי אליעזר says: If what he stole equals what he would sell for, he is sold. If not, he is not sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a thief whose value as a servant does not match the amount he stole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say that when the debt is bigger than his value, he can be sold a second time to pay the rest. When his value is bigger than the debt, he cannot be sold at all, since part of him cannot be sold. רבי אליעזר is stricter: the sale happens only when the two amounts are equal.

keyTerms.meaning: The value of what he stole
He is sold and then sold again
Equal to the price he would be sold for

steps.confusionAlert: Here the רבנן allow a second sale even for a single theft. That does not fit רבא's split in Step 17 or אביי's split in Step 19. In the next step, רבא sides with רבי אליעזר.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גְּנֵיבוֹ אֶלֶף, וְשָׁוֶה חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת –
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: If what he stole was worth a thousand and he is worth five hundred,
phrases.notes: "He is worth" means the price he would bring if sold as a servant.

phrases.english: he is sold and then sold again.
If what he stole was worth five hundred and he is worth a thousand,
he is not sold at all.
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה גְּנֵיבוֹ כְּנֶגֶד מִמְכָּרוֹ – נִמְכָּר,
phrases.english: If what he stole was equal to his sale price, he is sold;
and if not, he is not sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גְּנֵיבוֹ אֶלֶף, וְשָׁוֶה חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא about selling a thief more than once
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבנן: if the theft is worth more than he is, he is sold again; if it is worth less, he is not sold. רבי אליעזר: he is sold only when the theft equals his value.

steps.title: רבא: רבי אליעזר wins the argument
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows that the רבנן's own reason for not selling a thief worth more than his theft also forbids selling him for only part of his theft. So רבי אליעזר's view makes more sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: On this point רבי אליעזר beat the רבנן. Why do the רבנן say a thief who stole five hundred and is worth a thousand is not sold? Because the תורה says he is sold as a whole person, not half of him. In the same way, the תורה says he is sold for his theft, not for half of his theft.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא judges the argument in the ברייתא and says רבי אליעזר comes out on top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן agree that a thief worth more than his theft is not sold, because the Torah wants him sold whole, not partly. רבא points out that the same פסוק says he is sold "for his theft," meaning the whole theft. So a sale that covers only half the debt should not be allowed either, which is exactly רבי אליעזר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: He beat them; he won the argument
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
So too; the same reasoning applies

steps.whatToRemember: רבא uses the רבנן's own logic against them. If he cannot be sold for part of himself, he also cannot be sold for part of his theft. So רבי אליעזר wins.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move: taking a reason one side already accepts and showing it leads to the other side's position.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּהָא זְכָנְהוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: Rava said: In this, Rabbi Eliezer beat the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמַאי שְׁנָא גְּנֵיבוֹ חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת וְשָׁוֶה אֶלֶף
phrases.english: for what is different when he stole five hundred and is worth a thousand
that he is not sold?

phrases.aramaic: דְּנִמְכַּר כּוּלּוֹ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְלֹא חֶצְיוֹ,
phrases.english: Because the Torah said all of him is sold, and not half of him.
So too:
The Torah said he is sold for his theft,
and not sold for half of his theft.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּהָא זְכָנְהוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Judges the argument in the ברייתא from Step 20
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר's view is stronger. A thief is sold only for his entire theft, just as he is sold only as a whole person.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The reasoning 'all of him, not half of him' also means 'all of his theft, not half of it,' so a thief is sold only when his value equals his theft.

steps.title: רבא's first reading: against the master's will
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says she can be redeemed against 'his' will. רבא first assumes 'his' means the master (אדון).
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: they redeem her against his will. רבא thought this meant against the will of the master.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא and gives רבא's first guess about who 'his' refers to. This sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'his' in בעל כרחו is unclear, so it could mean the master or the father. רבא reads it as the master, which would mean the owner can be forced to let her go. The word סבר signals that this was only a first assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: he thought to say (a first assumption)

steps.confusionAlert: סבר רבא למימר means רבא only 'thought' this at first. It is not the final answer, and אביי is about to reject it.

phrases.english: And they redeem her against his will.
Rava thought to say
against the will of the master.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבַר רָבָא לְמֵימַר בְּעַל כֻּרְחֵיהּ דְּאָדוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the ברייתא about the אמה העבריה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First assumption: the master can be forced to accept her redemption.

steps.title: אביי: you can't force the master to take an IOU
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks how forcing the master would even work. It would mean giving him a promissory note for her value, which swaps a pearl for a shard.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What would it mean? That we write him a document for her value? Why should he accept that? He is holding a pearl in his hand, and we hand him a clay shard?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's reading. He argues it makes no sense to force the master to give up his maidservant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she has no money, the only way to free her against the master's will is to give him a debt document. The master already has her actual work, which is the 'pearl.' A document he cannot collect on right now is only a 'shard,' so it is unfair to force the trade.

keyTerms.meaning: a written document (here, a debt note)
a clay shard, something nearly worthless

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
What is it — that we write him
a document for her value?
phrases.notes: He means a debt note, so she goes free now and pays the master back later.

phrases.english: Why?
He is holding a pearl in his hand,
and we give him a clay shard?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that 'his will' means the master's will
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forcing the master would mean trading his valuable maidservant for an uncollectable debt note, which is unreasonable.

steps.title: אביי: against the father's will, because of family shame
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'his will' means the father's. He is pushed to redeem her because it shames the family.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: it means against the will of the father, because of the shame to the family.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his own reading of the ברייתא. The one forced is the father, not the master.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the master is not losing anything, because he gets paid in full. The pressure is on the father to come up with the money, since having a daughter serve as a maidservant is a disgrace to the family (פגם משפחה).

keyTerms.meaning: a blemish, or shame, on the family

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
against the will of the father,
because of the family's shame.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בְּעַל כֻּרְחֵיהּ דְּאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's rejected reading with a new one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The master is forced to free her.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father is pressured to redeem her because of the family's shame.

steps.title: Then force the family of a Hebrew slave too
steps.stepSummary: If family shame is the reason, the relatives of an עבד עברי should also be forced to redeem him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, for an עבד עברי too, let us force the family members to redeem him because of the family's shame!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's reason. It asks why the same logic doesn't apply to a Hebrew slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man sold as a slave also shames his family. If shame is enough to force the father here, it should force a slave's relatives too. Since we don't find that rule, the reason seems weak.

keyTerms.meaning: a Jewish man sold as a slave

phrases.english: If so, a Hebrew slave too,
let us force the family members
because of the family's shame!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's reason from step 24.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same shame exists for an עבד עברי, yet his family is not forced to redeem him.

steps.title: The slave would just sell himself again
steps.stepSummary: We don't force the slave's family, because he would go and sell himself again.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would go back and sell himself again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that forcing the family would be useless for an עבד עברי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man can sell himself over and over. If his family paid to free him, he could simply sell himself again and pocket the money at their expense. So forcing them accomplishes nothing.

phrases.english: He will go back and sell himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slave's family should be forced just like the father.
steps.terutzMaskana: Forcing them is pointless, since he could sell himself again.

steps.title: The father could also sell her again
steps.stepSummary: The same worry should apply to the father, who could sell his daughter a second time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the father would go back and sell her again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer around. It asks why forcing the father isn't also pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry about selling again stops us from forcing the slave's family, it should also stop us from forcing the father. He could take the redemption money and then sell her a second time.

phrases.english: Here too,
he will go back and sell her!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי הָדַר אָזֵיל וּמְזַבֵּין לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 26 to challenge the ruling of step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between the father and the עבד עברי's family
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The father can also sell again, so forcing him should be just as pointless.

steps.title: She cannot be sold a second time
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the ברייתא teaches a girl cannot be sold as a maidservant twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches: she is not sold a second time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the father has no option to sell her again, so forcing him is effective.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike a man who sells himself, a father may sell his daughter as a maidservant only once. Once she is redeemed, he cannot sell her again. So pressuring him to redeem her actually works.

keyTerms.meaning: sold and sold a second time

phrases.english: It teaches:
She is not sold and sold a second time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing a rule that removes the concern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father could sell her again, so forcing him is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: She cannot be sold twice, so forcing the father works.

steps.title: This follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The rule that she cannot be sold twice is רבי שמעון's view. A ברייתא shows the first opinion allows a second sale into servitude, while רבי שמעון forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון's. As it was taught: A person may sell his daughter for marriage and again, for servitude and again, and for marriage after servitude, but not for servitude after marriage. רבי שמעון says: just as a person may not sell his daughter for servitude after marriage, so too he may not sell his daughter for servitude after servitude.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies whose opinion the rule 'not sold twice' follows. It quotes a ברייתא where רבי שמעון holds this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion (תנא קמא) lets a father sell his daughter as a maidservant a second time. It only forbids servitude after marriage. רבי שמעון compares servitude after servitude to servitude after marriage and forbids both. So the rule in step 28 matches רבי שמעון.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's explanation, that the father is forced and the fear of a second sale doesn't apply, works according to רבי שמעון. In his view a daughter cannot be sold into servitude twice.

phrases.english: And whose is it? It is Rabbi Shimon's.
As it was taught:
A person may sell his daughter
for marriage and again,
for servitude and again,
phrases.notes: So this first opinion lets him sell her as a maidservant twice. That is exactly what רבי שמעון argues with.

phrases.english: for marriage after servitude,
but not for servitude after marriage.
Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין אָדָם מוֹכֵר אֶת בִּתּוֹ
phrases.english: Just as a person may not sell his daughter
for servitude after marriage,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אֵין אָדָם מוֹכֵר אֶת בִּתּוֹ
phrases.english: so too a person may not sell his daughter
for servitude after servitude.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the rule cited in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose opinion holds that she cannot be sold twice?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון, who forbids servitude after servitude, against the תנא קמא who allows it.

steps.title: This is a dispute of תנאים about 'בבגדו בה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the question of a second sale depends on a dispute among תנאים about the פסוק 'בבגדו בה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is in the dispute of these תנאים, as it was taught: 'בבגדו בה' (seeing he dealt deceitfully with her).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting another ברייתא. It is setting up a dispute about how to read the פסוק 'בבגדו בה,' which will explain the root of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we saw only that רבי שמעון and the תנא קמא disagree. Now the גמרא will show that this disagreement comes from different readings of the פסוק in שמות 21:8. The explanation continues in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: תנאים, the sages of the משנה era
'seeing he dealt deceitfully with her' (the פסוק about the father)

phrases.english: And it is in the dispute of these Tannaim,
as it was taught:
"Seeing he dealt deceitfully with her" —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Traces the dispute in step 29 back to a disagreement over a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The question of selling into servitude twice depends on how תנאים read 'בבגדו בה.'
